title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 59-61). M is a 'configuration': a set with combinatorial relations.
- ≤ is incidence: Y ≤ X means Y is a face of X.
- X̃ = {Y ≤ X} and ∂X = X̃ − {X}.
- X |∘| Y means 'disjoint interiors'.
- A further relation, written ≤ with a small circle (rendered '<<' in the previous-page transcription), means 'X lies in Y, interior inside interior'. It is meant for subdivision-type situations.

P is a space, and Figures(P) is the configuration of 'figures' in P. Grothendieck asks when a set-valued map X ↦ |X| (M → 𝒫(P)) comes from a homomorphism of configurations M → Figures(P). He defines |∂X| = ⋃_{Y<X} |Y| and |X|° = |X| \ |∂X|, and imposes four conditions:
- (i) X ≤° Y ⇒ |X| ⊂ |Y|.
- (ii) X |∘| Y ⇒ |X|° ∩ |Y|° = ∅.
- (iii) |X|° ≠ ∅.
- (iv) |X| = ⋃_{Y≤X} |Y|°.

This page does the verification.
1. For each X, the family (|Y|)_{Y∈X̃} is an elementary figure in the ambient |X|. Inclusions |Y| ⊂ |X| come from (i), applied only to the special case Y ≤ X. Elementarity follows from condition (iii) of the proposition on p. 37.
2. So f(X) := this family is well defined. f is compatible with ≤ (marginal reference to a condition on p. 28). For each X, f induces an isomorphism X̃ ≅ f(X), hence |X|° = f(X)°.
3. Consequently (ii) gives X |∘| Y ⇒ f(X) |∘| f(Y).
4. What remains is to show X ≤° Y ⇒ f(X) ≤° f(Y). One has a compatible map φ: X̃ → Ỹ with φ(X) = Y, subject to X' ≤° φ(X'). Everything reduces to |X|° ⊂ |Y|° (cross-reference to a condition 5 of an earlier text, pp. 19-20).
5. By (i), |X| ⊂ |Y|, so |X|° ⊂ |Y|.

The next page finishes the argument. It shows |X|° ∩ |Z|° = ∅ for all Z < Y, using (iv), (ii) and the axioms Mθ4 (Z < Y ⇒ Z |∘| Y) and Mθ3 (X ≤° Y, Y |∘| Z ⇒ X |∘| Z). It then states the theorem: homomorphisms M → Figures(P) correspond bijectively to maps X ↦ |X| satisfying (i)-(iv).

In modern terms, this is a 'stratified realization' criterion. A poset-indexed family of closed sets is the closed-cell system of a stratification exactly when:
- each closed cell is the disjoint union of the open cells of its faces;
- open cells are nonempty;
- open cells that are combinatorially 'disjoint' are disjoint;
- a subdivision-type relation forces open-cell inclusion.
It is analogous to recognizing face posets of regular cell complexes or cellular stratified spaces. It is a step in Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial-axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame/piecewise-linear topology) based on figures and configurations.
errors: Step 2 is asserted as 'il est clair' with a gap. That f induces an order isomorphism X̃ ≅ f(X) needs injectivity of Y ↦ |Y| and order reflection (|Y| ⊂ |Y'| ⇒ Y ≤ Y'). Some cases follow quickly: for Y < Y', equality |Y| = |Y'| would force |Y'|° = ∅, contradicting (iii). Incomparable pairs, however, require (ii) together with an axiom ensuring incomparable faces are |∘|-related. That axiom is presumably among the Mθ axioms or in the p. 37 proposition, but it is not visible here.
The derivation is incomplete on this page; it is completed correctly on p. 61. No mathematical error is visible.

ideas.what: Characterizing homomorphisms from an abstract configuration (poset with face, disjointness and 'interior-inclusion' relations) to the configuration of figures of a space. The characterization is via set-valued maps X ↦ |X| satisfying four stratification axioms (closed cell = union of open faces, nonempty interiors, disjointness, interior-inclusion).
ideas.modern_name: Geometric realization criterion for face posets / poset-stratified spaces (regular CW complexes, cellular stratified spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face posets of regular CW complexes: Björner (1984), Lundell-Weingram. Poset-stratified spaces: Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix), Tamaki (cellular stratified spaces).
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic mention of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished.

ideas.what: A relation ≤° ('interior inside interior'), distinct from the face relation, with axioms Mθ3/Mθ4 linking it to the disjointness relation |∘|. It is used to encode subdivision/refinement inside the combinatorial structure itself.
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision / refinement morphisms of stratifications, encoded combinatorially
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single source; PL topology subdivision theory (Zeeman, Rourke-Sanderson) treats this geometrically.

missed.claim: The page belongs to an unpublished axiomatic programme for tame topology ('analysis situs, quatrième mouture'). In it, cell structures and their subdivisions are encoded as 'configurations' with three relations (≤, |∘|, ≤°), and realizations are characterized by simple set-theoretic axioms. This combinatorial-axiomatic route to Esquisse-style tame topology seems not to have been developed in the literature. O-minimal tame topology took a different, model-theoretic route.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could inform purely combinatorial models of stratified spaces and subdivisions, for example exit-path categories and combinatorial models of PL/stratified homotopy theory. However, this particular page is a routine verification.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification step within an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself (configurations with an interior-inclusion relation, realization theorem) is of historical interest but is not individually striking.
